The '''2018–19 Ekstraklasa''' (also known as '''Lotto Ekstraklasa''' due to its [[Sponsor (commercial)|sponsorship]] by Totalizator Sportowy, Polish [[lottery]])<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.ekstraklasa.org/lotto-partnerem-tytularnym-ekstraklasy |title=LOTTO Partnerem Tytularnym Ekstraklasy |website=www.ekstraklasa.org |date=14 July 2016 |access-date=15 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160718034522/http://www.ekstraklasa.org/lotto-partnerem-tytularnym-ekstraklasy |archive-date=2016-07-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref> was the 93rd season of [[List of Polish football champions|the Polish Football Championship]], the 85th season of [[Sports league|the highest tier domestic division]] in the [[Polish football league system]] since its establishment in [[1927 Ekstraklasa|1927]] and the 11th season of the [[Ekstraklasa]] under its current title. The league was operated by the Ekstraklasa [[S.A. (corporation)|SA]].

The season started on 20 July 2018 and concluded on 19 May 2019.<ref name="Terminarz">{{cite web |url=http://www.90minut.pl/news/285/news2852811-Ramowy-terminarz-Ekstraklasy-2018-19.html |title=Ramowy terminarz Ekstraklasy 2018/19 |publisher = 90minut.pl |date=22 March 2018 |access-date=31 May 2018 |language=pl}}</ref> It is the second Ekstraklasa season to use [[Video assistant referee|VAR]]. After the 20th matchday the league went on a winter break between 23 December 2018 and 8 February 2019. The regular season was played as a [[round-robin tournament]]. A total of 16 teams participated, 14 of which competed in the league during the 2017–18 season, while the remaining two were promoted from the [[2017–18 I liga]]. The fixtures were announced on 22 March 2018.<ref name="Terminarz"/>

Each team played a total of 30 matches, half at home and half away. After the 30th round (in the beginning of April 2019), the league was split into two groups: ''championship round'' (top eight teams) and ''relegation round'' (bottom eight teams). Each team played 7 more games (teams ranked 1 to 4 and 9 to 12 played four times at home). Therefore, each team played a total of 37 matches. The team at the top of the Championship round won the league title. The two teams at the bottom of the Relegation round were relegated to [[2019–20 I liga]]. This was the sixth season to take place since the new playoff structure has been introduced.

The defending champions were [[Legia Warsaw]], who won their 13th Polish title [[2017–18 Ekstraklasa|the previous season]]. [[Piast Gliwice]] succeeded Legia, winning its first ever Polish top league title.

==Teams==
Sixteen teams competed in the league – the top fourteen teams from the previous season, as well as two teams promoted from the [[2017–18 I liga|I liga]]. [[Miedź Legnica]] were promoted to the Ekstraklasa for the first time.<ref>{{cite web | title = Miedź w Ekstraklasie | publisher = 90minut.pl | date = 27 May 2018 | url = http://www.90minut.pl/news/287/news2870264-Miedz-w-Ekstraklasie.html | access-date = 31 May 2018 }}</ref> [[Zagłębie Sosnowiec]] made a return to the [[Ekstraklasa]] for the first time since 2008.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.90minut.pl/news/287/news2870268-Zaglebie-Sosnowiec-w-Ekstraklasie.html |title=Zagłębie Sosnowiec w Ekstraklasie |publisher=90minut |date=27 May 2018 |access-date=31 May 2018 |language=pl}}</ref>
